source: NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch. 13 (Movements of Ocean Water).

sections.heading: 1. Waves and Tides
points: Ocean water moves in three ways: **waves, tides, and currents**.
**Waves** — caused by **wind**; energy moves, not the water itself; height depends on wind speed, duration and fetch.
**Tides** — the periodic **rise and fall of sea level** caused by the **gravitational pull of the Moon (and Sun)** plus the Earth's rotation.
**Spring tides** (highest) — Sun, Moon, Earth aligned (new/full moon); **Neap tides** (lowest) — Sun and Moon at right angles (quarter moon).

sections.heading: 2. Importance of Tides
points: Tides help in **navigation** (ships enter/leave ports), **fishing**, clearing sediment/silt at river mouths, and generating **tidal (electric) power**.
High tidal ranges occur in funnel-shaped inlets (e.g. Bay of Fundy).
Tides are highly predictable.

sections.heading: 3. Ocean Currents
points: **Currents** = large-scale movement of surface (and deep) water in definite directions.
Caused by: **prevailing winds, Coriolis force, temperature and salinity differences (density), Earth's rotation**.
Two types: **warm currents** (from equator toward poles) and **cold currents** (from poles toward equator).
Examples: **Gulf Stream** (warm, N. Atlantic), **Kuroshio** (warm, Pacific), **Labrador** (cold), **Humboldt/Peru** (cold), **Benguela** (cold), **Canary** (cold).

sections.heading: 4. Effects of Currents
points: Currents moderate **coastal climates** (warm currents warm coasts; cold currents cool/desert coasts).
Meeting of warm and cold currents creates **rich fishing grounds** (e.g. Grand Banks — Gulf Stream meets Labrador) but also **fog**.
Cold currents on west coasts of continents help form **deserts** (e.g. Atacama, Namib).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Waves caused by wind; tides by Moon's (and Sun's) gravity.
Spring tides = alignment (new/full moon, highest); Neap tides = right angle (quarter moon, lowest).
Currents: warm (equator→pole) and cold (pole→equator).
Gulf Stream & Kuroshio = warm; Labrador, Humboldt (Peru), Benguela = cold.
Warm + cold currents meet = rich fishing grounds (e.g. Grand Banks).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Spring tides** occur at **new and full moon** (Sun–Moon–Earth aligned) — highest.
**Neap tides** occur at the **quarter moon** (Sun and Moon at right angles) — lowest.
**Warm currents flow away from the equator**; cold currents toward it.
**Cold currents** along west coasts help form coastal **deserts** (Atacama, Namib).
